verses.1: The words that were spoken to Jeremiah, to all the Jews who lived in Egypt, those who lived in the mountains, in the valleys, and in the land of Patros.
verses.2: Thus said Jehovah, the God of Israel: “You have seen all the evil that I brought upon Jerusalem and all the cities of Judah. Today they are in ruins, and no one lives there anymore.”
verses.3: Because of their evil actions, which made me angry, they forced me to go and serve other gods. You and your ancestors do not know what those other gods are like.
verses.4: And I will send to you all my servants who are prophets. I will send them with this message: “Do not do what is evil, as I have commanded you.”
verses.5: And they did not hear, nor pay attention to their own sins. They refused to turn back from their evil ways, so as not to offend God in the eyes of others.
verses.6: My anger and my fury spread throughout the cities of Judah and the districts of Jerusalem. It became a time of destruction for them, just as it is today.
verses.7: And now, as Jehovah, the God of hosts and the God of Israel says: Why do you do such great harm to your own people? Why do you destroy men and women who are righteous and honest from among the Jews? I will not allow you to have any survivors.
verses.8: Let your actions provoke me. You come to this land of Egypt in order to serve other gods. You will be cursed and disgraced among all the nations of the earth.
verses.9: Have you forgotten the evils of your ancestors, and also the evils of the kings of Judah? Have you forgotten the evils of their wives, and the evils of those who lived in Jerusalem? These were the evils that they committed in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem.
verses.10: They have not obeyed until today. They do not fear me, nor do they walk in my laws and statutes that I gave you before, and before your ancestors.
verses.11: Therefore, as the Lord, the God of Israel, says: “I have turned my face against you with evil and destruction; I will destroy all of Judah.”
verses.12: And I took away the rest of the Jews who turned their faces towards Egypt, so that they could live there. But all of them died in Egypt. They died from hunger and disease. From a young age until old age, they died due to hunger and disease. They became objects of scorn and shame.
verses.13: And I took care of those who lived in Egypt, just as I took care of Jerusalem during the times of famine and plague.
verses.14: And they shall not be a remnant or survivors for the remaining Jews who come to that land in Egypt. They will return to the land of Judah, but they will not be able to settle there. They will not be able to return because they are already a “fleeing people.”
verses.15: And all the people who knew that their wives had been taken away by other gods, and all the women who stood in front of the crowd, and all the people who lived in Egypt at Pithom, answered:
verses.16: The words you have spoken to us in the name of Jehovah, we do not listen to you.
verses.17: For whatever was done, it will be done. All those things that came from us to serve the Queen of Heaven, and to provide her with offerings, as we and our ancestors have done. These offerings were made in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. We will also offer bread, and there will be both good and bad things that we will see.
verses.18: And from that time on, we stopped serving the queen of heaven. We no longer had any offerings to give her. In times of famine and starvation, we were left with nothing.
verses.19: And since we are destined to be the queens of heaven, and to serve her with sacrifices made by our people. We have prepared these sacrifices for her, so that she may enjoy them.
verses.20: And Jeremiah said to all the people, “To men and women, and to all those who hate him.”
verses.21: May the curse that has been placed upon you in the cities of Judah and in the suburbs of Jerusalem be removed from you, your ancestors, your kings, your priests, and all the people of this land. May Jehovah remember you and lift up His hand over you.
verses.22: And Jehovah could no longer bear to endure the insults and hardships that you have caused. Your land became a place of destruction, ruin, and desolation. There is no one who can save it today.
verses.23: Because you have sinned against Jehovah, and because you have not listened to His voice, His laws, His commands, and His statutes. Therefore, I call upon you for this evil that is happening today.
verses.24: And Jeremiah said to all the people and to all the women who had heard the words of Jehovah, to all the Jews who were in the land of Egypt:
verses.25: As Jehovah, the army of Israel’s God, said: “You and your descendants shall speak and act according to what you have been commanded. You shall do what is required of you. I will fulfill our covenant, which we made with her as queen of heaven. I will create for her sacrifices, and you shall also fulfill your own covenants.”
verses.26: Therefore, hear the words of the LORD, all of the Jews who live in the land of Egypt. I will bless my own name, the great name of the LORD. The LORD says, “If my name still remains known by anyone in all of Judea, then say: ‘May the LORD live in all the lands of Egypt!’”
verses.27: I will do them harm, not good. All the people of Judah will perish in Egypt, due to famine and disaster.
verses.28: And the exiles from Jerusalem will return from the land of Egypt, to the land of Judah. They will know all that has happened to Judah. Those who came from Egypt will dwell there. But nothing will be done to them or for them.
verses.29: And this is what the LORD says: I have appointed you to this place, so that you may know that My words will surely come true against you.
verses.30: So said Jehovah: “I will give Pharaoh Hophra to his enemies, and to those who seek to harm him. Just as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, so too will I give Pharaoh Hophra into the hands of his enemies.”
